external_entities.name: member
external_entities.description: A grocery loyalty programme member who uses the mobile app, signs in, approves consent, collects points and spends them on gift cards.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Members collect points when they shop and spend them on gift cards.

external_entities.name: member phone
external_entities.description: A member's phone on which the mobile app and its refresh token reside.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The app keeps a refresh token on the phone.

external_entities.name: browser
external_entities.description: A browser used by a member to sign in and approve consent, and to return an authorization code to a partner app.
external_entities.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.

external_entities.name: partner app
external_entities.description: A web application run by another company, such as a meal-planning service that shows a member's points.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

processes.name: mobile app
processes.description: The mobile app signs a member in through the authorization server and calls the rewards API with an access token.
processes.notes: The source does not state whether the app sends a PKCE challenge. A mobile refresh token never expires; each use slides its expiry forward another ninety days.

processes.name: authorization server
processes.description: The authorization server handles member sign-in, consent, authorization codes, refresh tokens and access tokens.
processes.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
processes.notes: The authorization server signs tokens for the support console with the same key.

processes.name: rewards API
processes.description: The rewards API accepts access tokens and reads and writes the points ledger.
processes.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger
processes.notes: Access tokens are signed JWTs, live for one hour, and are plain bearer tokens. The API does not check which client or audience a token was issued for.

processes.name: support console
processes.description: A web application that takes access tokens and closes a member's account.
processes.source_excerpt: The support console is a web app that closes a member's account.
processes.notes: It is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

data_stores.name: identity database
data_stores.description: Stores member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database, together with the authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents it issues.
data_stores.notes: Deleting a partner app's refresh token on disconnect does not affect an already-issued access token. Closing an account marks it closed here, while the member's refresh tokens remain.

data_stores.name: points ledger
data_stores.description: Stores every member's balance and every points transaction.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The ledger records which client made each change, and not which member approved it.

data_stores.name: API log store
data_stores.description: Stores every request received by the rewards API, including headers.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.

data_flows.name: use mobile app
data_flows.description: A member uses the mobile app.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Members use our mobile app.
data_flows.notes: unknown

data_flows.name: sign in
data_flows.description: The mobile app signs a member in through the authorization server using the authorization code flow.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The app signs a member in through our authorization server with the authorization code flow
data_flows.notes: The source does not state whether the app sends a PKCE challenge.

data_flows.name: call rewards API
data_flows.description: The mobile app calls the rewards API with the access token it receives.
data_flows.source_excerpt: then calls the rewards API with the access token it gets back
data_flows.notes: The access token is a plain bearer token.

data_flows.name: approve consent
data_flows.description: A member signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page and approves the consent screen listing scopes.
data_flows.source_excerpt: A member who connects a partner app signs in on the authorization server's sign-in page in their browser and approves a consent screen that lists the scopes.
data_flows.notes: unknown

data_flows.name: request token
data_flows.description: A partner app sends token requests containing its client secret in the request body.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The partner app sends that secret in the body of its token requests.
data_flows.notes: The authorization server accepts any redirect URI that starts with the registered redirect URI. Every partner app is given every scope.
data_flows.data_description: client ID, client secret and token request

data_flows.name: return code
data_flows.description: The browser returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The browser then returns to the partner app's redirect URI with an authorization code.
data_flows.notes: The authorization code stays valid for ten minutes.

data_flows.name: take access token
data_flows.description: The support console takes access tokens from the authorization server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It takes access tokens from the same authorization server
data_flows.notes: The source does not describe the token request interaction further.

data_flows.name: store identity data
data_flows.description: The authorization server stores and retrieves member identity and authorization data in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The authorization server keeps member accounts, email addresses and password hashes in the identity database
data_flows.notes: unknown
data_flows.data_description: member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents

data_flows.name: update points ledger
data_flows.description: The rewards API reads and writes balances and points transactions in the points ledger.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API reads and writes the points ledger, which holds every member's balance and every points transaction.
data_flows.notes: Redeeming points for a gift card needs only a valid access token carrying the redeem scope.

data_flows.name: write request logs
data_flows.description: The rewards API writes every received request, including headers, to the API log store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The rewards API also writes every request it receives, headers included, to the API log store.
data_flows.notes: unknown

data_flows.name: close account
data_flows.description: The support console marks a member's account closed in the identity database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Closing an account marks it closed in the identity database.
data_flows.notes: Closing an account does not remove the member's refresh tokens.

trust_boundaries.name: own cloud account
trust_boundaries.description: The organisation's cloud account in which the authorization server, rewards API, support console and stores run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account, apart from the members' phones and the partner apps.

trust_boundaries.name: members' phones
trust_boundaries.description: The member-controlled phones on which the mobile app runs and refresh tokens are kept.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Everything below runs in our own cloud account, apart from the members' phones and the partner apps.

trust_boundaries.name: partner apps' own servers
trust_boundaries.description: Servers controlled by other companies on which partner applications run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Partner apps are web applications that other companies run on their own servers

assumptions.assumption: The identity database contains confidential data because it stores member identifiers and authentication credentials.
assumptions.basis: The source states that it stores member accounts, email addresses, password hashes, authorization codes, refresh tokens and consents.

assumptions.assumption: The points ledger contains confidential data because it stores member-related balances and transactions.
assumptions.basis: The source states that it holds every member's balance and every points transaction.

assumptions.assumption: The API log store contains confidential data because it stores requests and headers, which may include credentials and member-related data.
assumptions.basis: The source states that every request received by the rewards API, headers included, is written to the store.

assumptions.assumption: The rewards API is internet-facing because it is served on the same public hostname as the support console.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.

assumptions.assumption: The support console is internet-facing because the source states that it is served on a public hostname.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the support console is served on the same public hostname as the rewards API.
